// why comfor

Composite Forming is complex.Your solver should stay transparent.

Comfor is an open-source explicit FEM solver designed for composite manufacturing research, where constitutive models, input files, and solver choices remain inspectable and reproducible.

— Traceable models.

Constitutive models are documented and linked to their source publications.

— Composite-first design.

Dry forming, thermostamping and RTM are treated as native use cases.

— Reproducible workflows.

Inputs, material parameters and solver settings can be versioned, shared and audited.

// simulation capabilities

What Comfor can simulate

A modular explicit FEM solver purpose-built for composite manufacturing. Each capability is backed by peer-reviewed constitutive models — no empirical shortcuts.

01 Manufacturing processes

Dry forming, thermostamping, draping, RTM, filament winding. Explicit non-linear FEM handles large deformations and transient dynamics throughout the forming cycle.

02 Composite material models

Woven fabrics, UD and NCF composites, anisotropic textile constitutive models, viscoplastic matrices. Every constitutive model links directly to its source publication.

03 Results & visualization

Stresses, displacements, fiber orientations, shear angles, and contact forces. Full ParaView integration for interactive post-processing and animation.

docs.title: Code of conduct
docs.text: This section details the coding style and formatting conventions used in the COMFOR project. These guidelines ensure consistency, readability, and long-term maintainability of the codebase.

docs.title: Key Conventions
docs.text:
COMFOR follows an adapted version of the LLVM coding style.

Aspect Standard Indentation 4 spaces (no tabs) Max line length 80 characters Brace style K&R / 1TBS Pointer alignment Left (int* ptr;) Namespace indentation None switch / case case aligned with switch File header Fixed format (see below) Enum declaration enum class Type aliases using (avoid typedef) Function/method names camelCase Class names PascalCase Private members snake_case_ File extensions .h and .cpp (no .hpp) Doxygen comments /// @ syntax only Required tools clang-format ≥ 15

For full details, refer to the .clang-format file in the project root.

docs.title: File Header Template
docs.text:
Every .h or .cpp file must start with the following header:

//------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// COMFOR - Simulation Framework for Composite Forming and Processing
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// @file        file_name.ext
// @brief       Description of the file content.
// @author      Your Name <your@email.com>
// @date        YYYY-MM-DD
// @copyright   (C) 20XX-20YY Your Name/University/Company
//
// For licensing terms, see the LICENSE file in the root directory.
//------------------------------------------------------------------------------

docs.title: VSCode Snippets
docs.text:
Predefined snippets are available in .vscode/comfor.code-snippets to quickly insert headers and separators.

How to use:

  1. Press Ctrl+Space to trigger snippets.
  2. Type the snippet name (e.g., comfor_hpp for a header file).
  3. Update placeholders (author, copyright, @brief).

Available snippets:

  • comfor_hpp → Header file template.
  • comfor_cpp → Source file template.
  • comfor_sep_long → Long separator.
  • comfor_sep_short → Section separator.
  • comfor_cmake_header → CMakeLists.txt header.

docs.title: CLion Live Templates
docs.text:
CLion automatically inserts COMFOR-style headers when creating new files (.cpp, .h, CMakeLists.txt). Templates are defined in .idea/fileTemplates.

Post-insertion steps:

  • Update author/contact information.
  • Adjust copyright years.
  • Complete Doxygen tags (e.g., @brief).

docs.title: Include What You Use (IWYU)
docs.text:
IWYU is integrated into COMFOR to optimize #include directives by:

  • Removing unused includes.
  • Adding missing includes.
  • Replacing internal Eigen includes with ComforMath.h.
  • Reducing build times and dependencies.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Windows Linux macOS

IWYU is not officially supported on Windows. Manual setup requires a full LLVM/Clang toolchain and building IWYU from source.

Debian/Ubuntu

sudo apt install include-what-you-use

Fedora

sudo dnf install include-what-you-use

Arch

sudo pacman -S include-what-you-use

Homebrew

brew install include-what-you-use

docs.title: Enable IWYU in CMake
docs.text:
Add the following to your CMakeLists.txt: 

option(USE_IWYU "Enable include-what-you-use analysis" ON)
if(USE_IWYU)
    find_program(IWYU_PATH NAMES include-what-you-use iwyu REQUIRED)
    set(CMAKE_CXX_INCLUDE_WHAT_YOU_USE
        ${IWYU_PATH}
        -Xiwyu --comment_style=long
        -Xiwyu --mapping_file=${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/.iwyu-imp)
endif()

docs.title: Manual Usage
docs.text:
Run IWYU manually with: 

python3 /usr/bin/iwyu_tool.py -p build \
  -- -Xiwyu --mapping_file=../.iwyu-imp > out.txt
Apply fixes with: 
python3 /usr/bin/fix_includes.py \
  --update_comments --reorder --nosafe_headers < out.txt

docs.title: Final Notes
docs.text:
1. Format your code with .clang-format before committing.
  2. Use official templates for headers and source files.
  3. Keep includes minimal with IWYU.
  4. Stay consistent with the project’s coding standards.

git config --global user.name "your_username"

git config --global --list

docs.title: Generate an SSH key pair
docs.text:
If you do not have an existing SSH key pair, generate a new one.

  1. Open a terminal.

  2. Type ssh-keygen -t followed by the key type and an optional comment. This comment is included in the .pub file that’s created. You may want to use an email address for the comment.

    For example, for ED25519:

    ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "<comment>"

  3. Press Enter. Output similar to the following is displayed:

$ ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Generating public/private ed25519 key pair.
Enter file in which to save the key (/home/user/.ssh/id_ed25519):

  • Accept the suggested filename and directory, unless you are generating a deploy key or want to save in a specific directory where you store other keys.

    You can also dedicate the SSH key pair to a specific host.

  • Specify a passphrase:

    Enter passphrase (empty for no passphrase):

A confirmation is displayed, including information about where your files are stored.

docs.title: Add an SSH key to your Git platform account
docs.text:
GitLab GitHub

To use SSH with GitLab, add your public key to your GitLab account settings.

  1. Copy the contents of your public key file. You can do this manually or use a script. For example, to copy an ED25519 key to the clipboard:

    macOS: 

    tr -d '\n' < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | pbcopy
    Linux (requires the xclip package): 
    xclip -sel clip < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
    Git Bash on Windows: 
    cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | clip

  2. Replace id_ed25519.pub with your filename. For example, use id_rsa.pub for RSA.

  3. Sign in to GitLab.
  4. In the top-left corner, select your avatar.
  5. Select Settings.
  6. From the left sidebar, select SSH Keys.
  7. In the Key box, paste the contents of your public key. If you manually copied the key, make sure you copy the entire key, which starts with ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa, and may end with a comment.
  8. In the Title text box, type a description, like Work Laptop or Home Workstation.
  9. Optional. In the Expires at box, select an expiration date. (Introduced in GitLab 12.9.) The expiration date is informational only, and does not prevent you from using the key. However, administrators can view expiration dates and use them for guidance when deleting keys.
  10. Select Add key.

To use SSH with GitHub, add your public key to your GitHub account settings.

  1. Copy the contents of your public key file. You can do this manually or use a script. For example, to copy an ED25519 key to the clipboard:

    macOS: 

    tr -d '\n' < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | pbcopy
    Linux (requires the xclip package): 
    xclip -sel clip < ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
    Git Bash on Windows: 
    cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | clip

  2. Replace id_ed25519.pub with your filename. For example, use id_rsa.pub for RSA.

  3. Sign in to GitHub.
  4. In the top-right corner, select your avatar.
  5. Select Settings.
  6. From the left sidebar, select SSH and GPG keys.
  7. Click New SSH key.
  8. In the Title field, add a descriptive label (e.g., Work Laptop or Home Workstation).
  9. In the Key field, paste your public key. Ensure the entire key is copied, starting with ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, or similar.
  10. Select Add SSH key.

docs.title: Temporal Semantics of the Explicit Solver
docs.text:
This page defines the temporal meaning of the main nodal quantities used by the explicit solver. It complements the theoretical presentation of the solver scheme with the timing contract used by the implementation.

Comfor uses a variable-step central-difference scheme in leapfrog form:

  • positions, displacements, rotations, forces, and accelerations live on integer times t^n
  • the primary velocity is staggered on half steps t^{n-1/2} and t^{n+1/2}

docs.title: Step context
docs.text:
The current increment is represented by:

  • time_n: current solver time t^n
  • dt_forward: forward drift interval Δt^{n+1/2}
  • dt_backward: previous drift interval Δt^{n-1/2}

Two derived quantities are used repeatedly:

\[ \Delta t^n = \frac{1}{2}\left(\Delta t^{n-1/2} + \Delta t^{n+1/2}\right) \]

and

\[ t^{n+1/2} = t^n + \frac{1}{2}\Delta t^{n+1/2} \]

The first quantity is the kick interval used to update the staggered velocity. The second is the time at which half-step velocity constraints are applied.

docs.title: Nodal field timing
docs.text:
The explicit solver uses the following interpretation:

Quantity Meaning Time instant position, displacement, rotation current configuration t^n velocity_half staggered velocity t^{n-1/2} on entry, t^{n+1/2} after the kick velocity_at_n reconstructed integer-step velocity t^n acceleration kick acceleration used by the solver t^n internal_force, external_force, contact_force, total_force assembled nodal forces t^n *_prev history fields previous-step values t^{n-1}

The distinction between velocity_half and velocity_at_n is essential:

  • velocity_half is used by the explicit integrator and by rate-dependent constitutive updates
  • velocity_at_n is used for nodal output and kinetic energy

docs.title: One explicit increment
docs.text:
One call to ExplicitSolver::solve() advances the solution from t^n to t^{n+1}.

The sequence is:

  1. choose the current dt_forward
  2. assemble nodal forces on the current configuration d^n
  3. compute nodal accelerations at t^n
  4. reconstruct the integer-step velocity v^n
  5. evaluate the current energy diagnostics
  6. save the converged n-state needed by the next increment
  7. kick the half-step velocity with Δt^n
  8. apply prescribed velocity constraints at t^{n+1/2}
  9. drift the configuration to d^{n+1} with Δt^{n+1/2}
  10. save the force history
  11. advance the solver clock to t^{n+1}

docs.title: Constitutive timing
docs.text: Constitutive updates follow two common patterns.

docs.title: Configuration-based path
docs.text: Material and section models based on the current geometry or deformation gradient are evaluated on the current configuration d^n. They therefore assemble stresses and internal forces at t^n.

docs.title: Rate-based path
docs.text:
Rate-based formulations use the staggered velocity on entry to the increment:

  • v^{n-1/2}
  • together with Δt^{n-1/2}

This defines the strain increment that closes at t^n and is then used to assemble the force state f^n.

docs.title: Velocity conventions
docs.text:
• velocity_half is the primary kinematic quantity for the explicit update
  • velocity_at_n is the reconstructed integer-step velocity used for output and energy evaluation

New code should avoid introducing an unnamed velocity quantity unless its time location is explicit.

docs.title: Initial state
docs.text:
Before the first increment:

  • the nodal state is reset to the reference configuration
  • prescribed velocity conditions at t = 0 are applied
  • prescribed acceleration conditions at t = 0 are applied

The first written state corresponds to this initialized configuration.

Acceleration-driven loads such as gravity are assembled during the first increment. The output written at t = 0 is therefore an initialized reference state, not a fully assembled dynamic state for those loads.

docs.title: Output timing
docs.text:
Comfor writes:

  • one initial output at t = 0
  • one output after each solved increment, according to the configured frequency

Each written state is labeled with its actual converged solver time.

Trackers reporting nodal velocity use the reconstructed integer-step velocity v^n, not the staggered half-step velocity.

docs.title: Energy diagnostics
docs.text:
The explicit solver tracks:

  • internal energy
  • external energy
  • kinetic energy
  • residual and balance indicators

These quantities remain useful, but damping dissipation and the work associated with prescribed kinematic conditions are not yet isolated as separate terms.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The explicit solver contract can be summarized as follows:

  • geometry and forces are evaluated at integer times t^n
  • the primary velocity is stored on staggered half steps
  • one increment assembles on d^n, kicks the half-step velocity, and drifts to d^{n+1}
  • rate-dependent updates use v^{n-1/2} and Δt^{n-1/2}
  • nodal velocity output uses the reconstructed integer-step velocity v^n
  • solved outputs are labeled with the actual converged time of the state

docs.title: Running the Analysis
docs.text: Once the model is defined in the input file, the next step is to execute COMFOR to perform the analysis. This section describes how to start a simulation, interpret the information displayed during execution, and understand the generated files.

docs.title: Basic Command
docs.text:
COMFOR is executed from the terminal (command line). The input file is given with the -j (or --job) option, which is required:

comfor -j <input_file> [OPTIONS]
  • <input_file>: Relative (to the current directory) or absolute path to the input file

Examples:

# File in the current directory
comfor -j simulation.toml

# Same, using the long option
comfor --job=simulation.toml

# Relative path
comfor -j ./simulations/forming.toml

# Absolute path
comfor -j /home/user/simulations/forming.toml

File Extensions

The input format is selected from the file extension:

Extension Format .toml, .giml TOML (recommended) .txt, .in Fembic (legacy)

docs.title: Command Line Options
docs.text: The options below are the ones printed by comfor --help.

docs.title: Job Options
docs.text: Option Description -j, --job INPUT_FILE_NAME Input file name (required). -o, --output PATH Result root directory. Replaces the default Results_<input_name>/ directory. Relative paths are resolved from the current directory. --validate Parse and validate the input file without running the simulation. -u, --cpus 1 Number of CPUs. The current build is serial: only 1 is accepted (default). Contact Innovamics for more capacity.

docs.title: Application Options
docs.text:
Option Description -i, --info Show general information about COMFOR -c, --credits Show software credits, contributors and third-party libraries -l, --license Show software license -v, --version Display COMFOR version and exit -h, --help Display the help message and exit

Usage examples:

# Only validate the input file
comfor -j simulation.toml --validate

# Run the simulation
comfor -j simulation.toml

# Write the results below a custom directory
comfor -j simulation.toml -o ./results/run-01

# Validate, then run only if the validation succeeded
comfor -j simulation.toml --validate && comfor -j simulation.toml

# Show version
comfor --version

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
When the --validate option is used, COMFOR:

  1. Parses the input file (TOML syntax errors are reported with their line number)
  2. Validates every block: mandatory parameters, parameter types, allowed values and ranges
  3. Checks that names are present and unique within each block type
  4. Writes the report to the terminal and to the job log, then exits without running the simulation

Checks that require the model to be built (for instance that the sections assigned to a set are compatible with its element types, or that referenced sets exist) are performed when the simulation starts.

Tip

The same validation is always performed at the beginning of a normal run: --validate is simply a fast way to check a file without creating any result.

Quasi-static simulations

For forming processes, which are quasi-static, the kinetic energy should remain small compared to the internal energy once the deformation has started. A large Ek/Ei ratio indicates significant dynamic effects (tool speed too high, not enough damping, etc.). docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
For an input file simulation.toml:

simulation.toml
simulation.md                  # Job log
Results_simulation/            # Result root (or the path given with -o)
├── manifest.toml              # Run status and list of generated files
├── <output_name>/             # One folder per [[output]] block
│   ├── <output_name>_000000.vtu
│   ├── <output_name>_000001.vtu
│   └── ...
└── <tracker_name>.csv         # One file per [tracker] block
  • Each [[output]] block writes its frames in a folder named after the output name. Frames are numbered with 6 digits.
  • Each [tracker] block writes one CSV file named after the tracker name.
  • manifest.toml records the run status (running, completed or failed) and the list of files written.

Existing results

The result root must not exist before the run. If it does, COMFOR stops with a Directory already exists error to avoid overwriting previous results. Delete the directory or choose another one with -o.

docs.title: Job Log
docs.text:
The job log is a Markdown file written next to the input file, with the same name (simulation.md for simulation.toml). It contains the same information as the terminal (file info, validation report, model summary, frames) and, when the validation fails, the full list of errors under Validation Errors.

See Post-processing for the content of the result files.

docs.title: Error Types
docs.text:
1. Command line errors: Missing -j or unknown option (COMFOR prints the error and the hint Run with --help for more information.), or input file not found.
  2. Parsing errors: Invalid TOML syntax, or block without a required name. The message gives the line number.
  3. Validation errors: Missing or invalid parameters. All errors are listed in the job log.
  4. Setup errors: Problems found while building the model (missing reference, incompatible section, existing result directory...).

docs.title: Error Message Format
docs.text:
--> Exception caught
Validation failed
  --> TOMLParser: block 'output' at line 14 requires a non-empty 'name'.

 --> Exception caught
Setup failed
  --> Directory already exists: /home/user/simulations/Results_simulation

In both cases COMFOR exits with a non-zero status code, which can be used in scripts.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Validate before execution: comfor -j file.toml --validate
  2. Start small: Test with a reduced model or a short run_to
  3. Monitor energies: Keep Ek/Ei small for quasi-static processes
  4. Check units: Ensure unit consistency (see Units)

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
# Validate
comfor -j forming.toml --validate

# Run, writing the results below ./results/forming
comfor -j forming.toml -o ./results/forming

# Check results
ls ./results/forming
cat ./results/forming/manifest.toml

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Comfor is an explicit non linear finite element software for composite modelling modelling. It is suitable for dynamic transient response and some quasi static problems by using dynamic relaxation.

The different materials, finite elements, contact laws come from confirmed and recent research works.

docs.text: After successfully running a COMFOR simulation, results are available in various formats for analysis and visualization. This section explains how to access, visualize, and analyze your simulation results.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
For an input file simulation.toml with an output named fields and two trackers named PunchForce and CenterPosition:

Project_Folder/
├── simulation.toml              # Input file
├── simulation.md                # Job log
└── Results_simulation/          # Result root (or the path given with -o)
    ├── manifest.toml            # Run status and list of files
    ├── fields/                  # One folder per [[output]], named after it
    │   ├── fields_000000.vtu
    │   ├── fields_000001.vtu
    │   └── ...
    ├── PunchForce.csv           # One CSV file per [tracker], named after it
    └── CenterPosition.csv
  • Frames are written every frequency time units and numbered with 6 digits, starting at 000000 (initial state).
  • When several [[output]] blocks are defined, each one writes in its own folder.

docs.title: Run Manifest
docs.text:
manifest.toml is updated during the run. Its status is running during the simulation, then completed or failed. It also lists every file written (path, format and size):

schema_version = 1
status = 'completed'

[[artifacts]]
channel_id = 'fields'
format = 'vtu'
path = 'fields/fields_000000.vtu'
size = 34305

Checking status = 'completed' is a simple way to verify, in a script, that a simulation ended normally.

docs.title: Job Log
docs.text: The job log simulation.md is a Markdown file written next to the input file. It contains the file information, the validation report (with the list of errors if any), the model summary and the energies printed at each output frame. See Running the Analysis.

docs.title: VTU Format (Recommended)
docs.text:
VTU (XML Unstructured Grid) is the recommended output format for COMFOR. Legacy VTK is still supported. Both are industry standards for scientific visualization.

Feature VTU VTK (legacy) ASCII encoding Yes Yes BINARY encoding (zlib compressed) Yes No Element results (strain, stress, fibers, resultants) Yes Yes Identifiers (MaterialID, PartID, PartInstanceID) Yes No

Configuration example:

[[output]]
name = "fields"
type = "VTU"
format = "BINARY"  # or "ASCII"
frequency = 0.1    # Write every 0.1 time units

Recommendation

Use BINARY for production simulations to reduce file size. Use ASCII to inspect the files with a text editor.

docs.title: Nodal Data (Point Data)
docs.text:
Data Components Description Displacement 3 Displacement \([u_x, u_y, u_z]\) Velocity 3 Velocity \([v_x, v_y, v_z]\) Acceleration 3 Acceleration \([a_x, a_y, a_z]\) Force 3 Resultant nodal force ContactForce 3 Nodal contact force SlidingVelocity 3 Contact sliding velocity

The node coordinates are stored as the mesh points (Position in the file).

docs.title: Element Data (Cell Data)
docs.text:
Data Components Description MaterialID 1 Material identifier PartID 1 Part identifier, starting at 0, in alphabetical order of the part names ([part.Name] syntax) PartInstanceID 1 Instance identifier inside a part (see pattern) Strain 6 Strain in the element local frame GreenLagrangeStrain 6 Green-Lagrange strain tensor DeformationGradient 9 Deformation gradient \(\mathbf{F}\) CauchyStress 6 Cauchy stress tensor ShearAngle 1 In-plane shear angle of the fabric (composite materials) FiberStrain 2 Strain along the warp and weft directions (composite materials) FiberStress 2 Stress along the warp and weft directions (composite materials) FiberCurvature 2 Curvature along the warp and weft directions (composite materials) FiberOrientationWarp 3 Current warp direction (composite materials) FiberOrientationWeft 3 Current weft direction (composite materials) ResultantN 3 Membrane force resultants \(N_{xx}, N_{yy}, N_{xy}\) (shell sections) ResultantM 3 Bending moment resultants \(M_{xx}, M_{yy}, M_{xy}\) (shell sections) ResultantQ 2 Transverse shear resultants \(Q_x, Q_y\) (shell sections)

Unavailable values

A field that does not apply to an element is written as NaN for that element: for instance all the stress and strain fields of rigid contact elements, or the fiber fields of non-composite materials. ParaView shows these elements with the NaN color and ignores them in the data range.

docs.title: Tensor Components
docs.text:
Field Component order ParaView labels CauchyStress, GreenLagrangeStrain xx, yy, zz, xy, yz, xz Identical DeformationGradient xx, xy, xz, yx, yy, yz, zx, zy, zz Identical Strain C11, C22, C33, C23, C13, C12 XX, YY, ZZ, XY, YZ, XZ

Components of Strain

ParaView labels the components of Strain with its own convention: the component displayed as XY is C23, YZ is C13 and XZ is C12. The same component names (C11...C12) are used by the STRAIN element tracker.

In legacy VTK files, the element fields are written as a FIELD block with the same names and component orders.

docs.title: Visualization with ParaView
docs.text: ParaView is the recommended visualization tool for COMFOR results.

docs.title: Load the Files
docs.text:
Click on File → Open and navigate to the folder of your output (e.g. Results_simulation/fields/). Since COMFOR names files in ascending order (fields_..vtu), ParaView automatically proposes to open them as a file group (time series).

Loading the files

docs.title: Play the Animation
docs.text:
After opening the files, they appear in the Pipeline Browser. Click the Apply button in the Properties section to render the mesh.

Workflow Hint

To save time, activate Auto Apply in Edit → Settings → General → Properties Panel Options.

To play the animation, use the Play button on the VCR toolbar. You can navigate frame by frame, loop the animation, or jump to specific time steps using the time toolbar.

The data to be displayed can be selected in the Coloring dropdown menu of the Properties panel. You can visualize nodal data (e.g. Displacement) or element data (e.g. CauchyStress, ShearAngle), and choose the component or the magnitude.

Playing the animation

Deformed shape

The mesh points are written at their current position: the geometry displayed in ParaView is already the deformed one. The Displacement field can be used to color the mesh, or with the Warp By Vector filter to amplify the deformation.

docs.title: Applying Filters
docs.text:
ParaView provides a wide range of filters to process and analyze simulation data. Filters can be stacked in the Pipeline Browser to combine effects.

Commonly used filters for COMFOR simulations:

Filter Use Threshold Extract the elements whose value lies in a range (e.g. PartID to isolate a part, or ShearAngle to find the highly sheared zones) Connectivity Identify connected regions, e.g. to separate the tools from the composite plates Cell Data to Point Data Average element data at the nodes (smoother contour plots) Warp By Vector Amplify a deformation using a vector field Temporal Interpolator Interpolate between frames, for smooth animations Plot Data Over Time Plot the time evolution of a selection Plot Data Plot data arrays, e.g. the content of a tracker CSV file Applying filters

docs.title: CSV Files (Trackers)
docs.text: Trackers record the time history of specific variables in CSV files, one file per tracker: <result_root>/<tracker_name>.csv. A row is written each time an output frame is written.

docs.title: CSV File Format
docs.text:
• Header line: Time, one column per tracked entity, then Total
  • Separator: comma followed by a space (,)
  • Total: sum of the values of all tracked entities

Example (NODE tracker, variable = "FORCE", direction = "Z"):

Time, Node 101, Node 102, Node 103, Total
0, 0, 0, 0, 0
0.1, 50.2, 48.7, 52.1, 151
0.2, 100.5, 95.3, 105.8, 301.6

Example (ELEMENT tracker, variable = "CAUCHY_STRESS", component = "xx"):

Time, Element 50, Element 51, Element 52, Total
0, 0, 0, 0, 0
0.1, 15.2, 18.1, 14.5, 47.8
0.2, 20.1, 22.5, 19.8, 62.4

docs.title: CSV Analysis with Python
docs.text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# skipinitialspace removes the space after each comma
df = pd.read_csv('Results_simulation/PunchForce.csv', skipinitialspace=True)

plt.plot(df['Time'], df['Total'], label='Punch force')
plt.xlabel('Time')
plt.ylabel('Force')
plt.grid(True)
plt.legend()
plt.show()

Force-displacement curve, with a NODE tracker on the punch force and a POSITION tracker on a punch node:

force = pd.read_csv('Results_simulation/PunchForce.csv', skipinitialspace=True)
position = pd.read_csv('Results_simulation/PunchPosition.csv', skipinitialspace=True)

# Punch displacement from its initial position
displacement = position['Total'].iloc[0] - position['Total']

plt.plot(displacement, force['Total'])
plt.xlabel('Punch displacement')
plt.ylabel('Punch force')
plt.show()

The corresponding trackers:

[tracker.PunchForce]
type = "NODE"
variable = "FORCE"
direction = "Z"
set = "PunchNodes"

[tracker.PunchPosition]
type = "NODE"
variable = "POSITION"
direction = "Z"
nodes = [50]

The CSV files can also be opened directly in ParaView (with the Plot Data filter), Excel or LibreOffice Calc.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Solution No time series detected in ParaView Open the files from the output folder (Results_<name>/<output_name>/) and select the ..vtu group A Strain component is not the expected one Check the component order (see Tensor Components) Some elements are drawn with the NaN color The field does not apply to these elements (e.g. rigid tools, fiber fields of non-composite materials) KeyError: 'Total' with pandas Use skipinitialspace=True in read_csv manifest.toml status is failed Read the error at the end of the job log (<input_name>.md)

docs.title: Preprocessing
docs.text:
COMFOR defines the numerical model through a structured input file. The framework features a modular parser architecture 1 supporting both the modern TOML standard (recommended for its modularity and readability) and the legacy Fembic format (maintained for backward compatibility).

Unlike previous versions, COMFOR now decouples the geometric definition from the physical properties, allowing the direct import of external mesh formats such as Abaqus (.inp) or Gmsh (.msh), alongside Inline definitions.

In the general case, a complete input file must define the following core pillars:

  • Geometry & Assembly: Definition of mesh sources (Mesh) and their assembly into physical components (Part).
  • Material Properties: Constitutive laws and physical data assigned to the parts.
  • Boundary Conditions: Kinematic constraints (Constraints) applied to the model.
  • Loads: External solicitations such as punctual forces, pressures, or gravity.
  • Analysis Control: Simulation time range, time-stepping settings, and output frequency.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
There is no predefined unit system in COMFOR. The user can use any consistent unit system see reference. The units must be consistent in that mathematical operations directly yield the correct units for the result quantity. For example for Newtons' law :

\[ \mathbf{f} = \mathbf{M} \mathbf{a} \]

If the unit force is the the newton \(N\), the length unit is the \(mm\) and the time unit is the second \(s\), the units for acceleration are \(mm/s^2\) and the units for mass, must be \(kg \cdot 10^{3} = t\) (metric ton).

docs.title: Input Structure
docs.text:
The configuration file is organized into Blocks. Each block corresponds to a specific category of data (a label) and defines the properties of a model component.

Naming

Every block requires a Name, except control and solver. This name acts as a handle that allows different parts of the simulation to talk to each other. For example, you define a material named "Steel", and then a section references "Steel" to know which constitutive law to use.

Names must be unique within a block type (two materials cannot share the same name, but a set and a surface can). Some names are also used for result files: the name of an output is the name of its result folder, and the name of a tracker is the name of its CSV file.

Available Blocks Block Syntax Required Multiple Description control [control] Yes No Simulation time range and time step solver [solver] No No Time integration settings output [[output]] Yes Yes Result files (VTU/VTK) mesh [mesh.Name] Yes* Yes Geometric sources part [part.Name] Yes* Yes Physical components built from meshes set [set.Name] No Yes Groups of nodes or elements surface [surface.Name] No Yes Merged sets used by contacts material [material.Name] No Yes Constitutive laws section [section.Name] No Yes Physical properties (thickness, radius...) section_assignments [[section_assignments]] No Yes Links sections to element sets amplitude [amplitude.Name] No Yes Time functions constraint [constraint.Name] No Yes Boundary conditions load [load.Name] No Yes Forces, pressures, body accelerations contact_behaviour [contact_behaviour.Name] No Yes Normal and tangential contact laws contact [contact.Name] No Yes Contact interactions tracker [tracker.Name] No Yes Time histories in CSV files

*At least one mesh and one part are needed to define the geometry of the model.

Note

section_assignments is the only block name written in the plural form.

Numbers

Write real-valued parameters as floating-point numbers (10.0 rather than 10), as in all the examples of this documentation.

Block Syntax

Depending on the format, the way you declare these blocks and their names differs.

TOML Fembic

In TOML, we strongly recommend using Keyed Tables. This syntax is more concise and clearly highlights the unique name of the object in the header.

# Recommended Syntax (Keyed Table)
[label.UniqueName]
type = "SPECIFIC_TYPE"
parameter = value

Example: 

[material.Steel_S235]
type = "ELASTIC"
young = 210000.0

Alternative Syntax

You can also use the array syntax [[label]] with a name = "..." field inside. Both syntaxes are equivalent and can be mixed in the same file. The keyed version [label.Name] is preferred for clarity, while the array syntax is commonly used for [[output]] and [[section_assignments]].

[[material]]
name = "Steel_S235"
type = "ELASTIC"
young = 210000.0

In the legacy format, the block starts with the label and the technology type. The entries follow on the subsequent lines, starting with their unique name.

LABEL TYPE SPECIFIC_TYPE
UniqueName parameter = value

Example: 

MATERIALS TYPE ELASTIC
Steel_S235 YOUNG = 210000.0

Order of Operations

The order of blocks in the input file does not impact the parsing. COMFOR loads all definitions into a registry before "linking" them together. However, keeping a logical flow (Control → Geometry → Physics → Trackers) is recommended for maintenance.

docs.title: Control
docs.text: The control block defines the global time parameters for the simulation, managing the analysis duration and the time integration strategy.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description run_to Float Yes - Final simulation time. Must be non-negative. run_from Float No 0.0 Starting time of the analysis. Must be non-negative. time_step Float No - Fixed time increment. Must be strictly positive if specified. If omitted, COMFOR uses an automatic stable time step based on the mesh and materials.

Validation Rule

The value of run_from must be strictly less than run_to. If this condition is not met, the simulation will fail during the validation phase with a ControlStep error.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Typical setup with automatic time-stepping
[control]
run_from = 0.0
run_to = 15.0

# Setup with a fixed manual time-step
[control]
run_to = 10.0
time_step = 0.0001

CONTROLS
RUN FROM 0.0 TO 15.0

CONTROLS
RUN TO 10.0 STEP 0.0001

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The output block defines the results generation settings, including the format and frequency of the output files. At least one output is required. You can define multiple outputs to export different formats or frequencies simultaneously.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description name String Yes - Name of the output. The frames are written in <result_root>/<name>/<name>_000000.vtu, ..._000001.vtu, etc. frequency Float Yes - Time interval between two result frames. Must be positive. type String No VTU Export format. Available: VTU (recommended) or VTK. format String No ASCII Data encoding. Available: ASCII or BINARY.

The result root is Results_<input_name>/ next to the input file, or the directory given with the -o command line option.

Format Compatibility

The legacy VTK type does not support BINARY encoding. If you need binary exports for better performance and smaller file sizes, please use the VTU type.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Standard binary output, written in Results_<input_name>/fields/
[[output]]
name = "fields"
type = "VTU"
format = "BINARY"
frequency = 0.1

# Additional ASCII output for debugging, written in Results_<input_name>/debug/
[[output]]
name = "debug"
type = "VTU"
format = "ASCII"
frequency = 0.5

OUTPUT
TYPE = VTU FREQUENCY = 0.1 FORMAT = BINARY

OUTPUT
TYPE = VTU FREQUENCY = 0.5 FORMAT = ASCII

docs.title: Mesh
docs.text:
TOML Only

This block is specific to the TOML configuration format. In the legacy Fembic format, geometry and physical properties are defined directly within the NODES and ELEMENTS blocks.

The mesh block defines the geometric source of your model. COMFOR can either read external files from standard pre-processors or define geometry "inline" for simple cases.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Reader engine: ABAQUS, GMSH, FEMBIC or INLINE. file String Yes* - Path to the external file, absolute or relative to the directory of the input file. Required for GMSH and ABAQUS. nodes Array Yes* - List of nodes [id, x, y, z]. Required only for INLINE type. elements Array No - List of elements [id, "TYPE", n1, n2, ...]. See Element Module for available types. Only for INLINE type.

docs.title: Element Type Translation
docs.text:
External readers translate the native element types into COMFOR element types (default translation). Any element type can be changed per part with element_mapping.

ABAQUSGMSHINLINE Abaqus type (*ELEMENT, TYPE=) COMFOR type T3D2 ROD_2 M3D3 MEMBRANE_3 S3, S3R S3L_C0 STRI3 DKT18 Any other type No default: must be mapped with element_mapping (e.g. R3D3)

Only the *NODE and *ELEMENT keywords are read; other keywords are ignored.

Gmsh element type COMFOR type 1 (2-node line) ROD_2 2 (3-node triangle) MEMBRANE_3

Other Gmsh element types have no default translation and must be mapped with element_mapping.

The element type is written directly in the elements array and must be a COMFOR element type.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
External FileInline Definition 
[mesh.BodyMesh]
type = "GMSH"
file = "models/chassis.msh"

[mesh.SimpleSquare]
type = "INLINE"
nodes = [
    [1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
    [2, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
    [3, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0],
    [4, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0]
]
elements = [
    [1, "MEMBRANE_3", 1, 2, 3],
    [2, "MEMBRANE_3", 3, 4, 1]
]

docs.title: Part
docs.text:
TOML Only

This block is specific to the TOML configuration format. In the legacy Fembic format, geometry and physical properties are defined directly within the NODES and ELEMENTS blocks.

A part represents a physical component. It instantiates a geometric source defined in a [mesh] block and applies global spatial transformations or element type mappings.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description mesh String Yes - Name of the [mesh] block to be used. translation Array No* [0,0,0] Global translation vector [tx, ty, tz]. Cannot be used with pattern. pattern Array No* - List of pattern configurations for duplicated placements. Cannot be used with translation. element_mapping Map No - Dictionary { "FROM" = "TO" } assigning a COMFOR element type to the element types of the mesh.

Exclusivity Rule

The translation and pattern parameters are mutually exclusive. Specifying both on the same part will result in a validation error.

docs.title: Pattern Parameters (Linear)
docs.text:
When using the pattern array, each pattern definition supports the following keys:

Parameter Type Required Description type String Yes Pattern geometry type. Supported: LINEAR. translation Array Yes Base translation vector [tx, ty, tz] for the pattern origin. count Integer Yes Number of instances to generate (must be positive). spacing Float Yes Distance between consecutive instances (must be positive). direction Array Yes Direction vector [dx, dy, dz] for pattern propagation (cannot be zero, normalized internally).

Instance i (starting at 0) is placed at translation + i × spacing × direction. Several patterns can be listed in the same part; their instances are added. Sets referring to a patterned part with ids or range select these IDs in every instance.

docs.title: Element Mapping Syntax
docs.text:
The keys of element_mapping are the element types as written in the mesh file: the Abaqus type ("S3", "R3D3"...) or the Gmsh type number as a string ("2"). The COMFOR type given by the default translation (e.g. "MEMBRANE_3") is also accepted as a key. When both match, the mesh file type takes precedence. Element types not listed in the mapping keep their default translation.

There are two ways to define the element_mapping in TOML:

  1. Inline Table: Useful for short mappings.
  2. Nested Table: Better for clarity when mapping many element types.
1. Inline Table2. Nested Table 
[part.Tool]
mesh = "AbaqusInp"
element_mapping = { "S3" = "CONTACT_TRIANGLE", "R3D3" = "CONTACT_TRIANGLE" }

[part.Tool]
mesh = "AbaqusInp"

[part.Tool.element_mapping]
"S3"   = "CONTACT_TRIANGLE"
"R3D3" = "CONTACT_TRIANGLE"

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Defining a physical part with a translation from a mesh source
[part.MainPlate]
mesh = "PlateGeometry"
translation = [0.0, 0.0, 50.0]

# Duplicating a mesh using a linear pattern (5 instances along X)
[part.Stiffeners]
mesh = "RibMesh"
[[part.Stiffeners.pattern]]
type = "LINEAR"
translation = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
count = 5
spacing = 20.0
direction = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Mapping element types for imported mesh formats
# (Gmsh 3-node triangles are type 2)
[part.Chassis]
mesh = "GmshMesh"
[part.Chassis.element_mapping]
"2" = "S3L_C0"

Implicit Parts

In Fembic, parts are not explicitly defined. Properties like material and thickness are assigned directly within the ELEMENTS block.

ELEMENTS TYPE MEMBRANE_3
1 NODES = [1, 2, 3] MATERIAL = Steel_S235 T = 1.2

docs.title: Section
docs.text:
TOML Only

This block is specific to the TOML configuration format. In the legacy Fembic format, geometry and physical properties are defined directly within the NODES and ELEMENTS blocks.

The section block defines specific physical properties (such as thickness, integration points, or radius) linked to a material model. Physical sections are then assigned to element sets using the [[section_assignments]] list.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Section formulation type: ROD, MEMBRANE, SHELL_GAUSS, SHELL_GENERALIZED or RIGID. material String Yes* - Name of the Material. Required for all types except RIGID.

The other parameters (thickness, radius, nip, integration, geometry) depend on the type: see the Section Module. The section type must be compatible with the element types of the set it is assigned to (e.g. ROD for ROD_2, RIGID for contact elements).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Gauss shell section definition
[section.SEC_SHELL]
type = "SHELL_GAUSS"
material = "Composite_Material"
thickness = 2.5
nip = 5
integration = "GAUSS"

# Assigning the section to an element set
[[section_assignments]]
name = "AssignShell"
section = "SEC_SHELL"
set = "ReinforcedSet"

Implicit Logic

Fembic does not have a "Section" concept. Variations in properties must be defined line-by-line within the ELEMENTS block.

ELEMENTS TYPE MEMBRANE_3
1 NODES=[1,2,3] MATERIAL=Steel T=1.2
2 NODES=[4,5,6] MATERIAL=Steel T=5.0  # Equivalent to a manual section change

docs.title: Section Assignment
docs.text:
TOML Only

This block is specific to the TOML configuration format. In the legacy Fembic format, physical properties are defined directly within the ELEMENTS block.

The section_assignments block links a defined Section to an element Set. It acts as the mapping layer that applies geometric and constitutive definitions to specific regions of the model mesh.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description name String Yes - Unique name of the assignment. section String Yes - Name of the Section to assign. set String Yes - Name of the target element Set. Must be a set of type ELEMENT.

Validation Rule

The referenced set must exist and be defined as an ELEMENT set. Referencing a NODE set will result in a validation error during the linking phase.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Section assignment using array of tables syntax
[[section_assignments]]
name = "AssignMembrane"
section = "SEC_MEMBRANE"
set = "MainBodyElements"

# Keyed table syntax is also supported
[section_assignments.AssignBending]
section = "SEC_SHELL"
set = "RibElements"

Implicit Logic

In Fembic, section assignments do not exist as separate blocks. Physical properties are specified line-by-line inside the ELEMENTS block.

ELEMENTS TYPE MEMBRANE_3
1 NODES = [1, 2, 3] MATERIAL = Steel T = 1.0

docs.title: Nodes (Legacy)
docs.text:
Fembic Only

This block is specific to the Fembic legacy format. In TOML, nodes are typically defined within a [mesh] block or using the nodes array in an INLINE mesh.

The NODES block defines the coordinates of each point in the model and can optionally assign boundary conditions or loads directly to them.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description ID Integer Yes - Unique identifier for the node (first token). X, Y, Z Float Yes - Spatial coordinates of the node. CONSTRAINT String No - Name of a Constraint to apply to this node. LOAD String No - Name of a nodal Load to apply to this node.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
NODES
1   X = 0.0  Y = 0.0  Z = 0.0  CONSTRAINT = FixedBase
2   X = 10.0 Y = 0.0  Z = 0.0  LOAD = PunctualForce
3   X = 5.0  Y = 5.0  Z = 0.0

Implicit Sets

When you assign a CONSTRAINT or a LOAD directly in the NODES block, COMFOR automatically creates an internal Set containing all nodes sharing that same constraint or load name.

docs.title: Elements (Legacy)
docs.text:
Fembic Only

This block is specific to the Fembic legacy format. Elements in Fembic are "physical": they contain both connectivity and physical properties (material, thickness).

The ELEMENTS block defines the connectivity and the physical behavior of the mesh. All elements within a single block must share the same Technology Type.

docs.title: Block Header
docs.text:
ELEMENTS TYPE <TECHNOLOGY>

See the Element Module for available technologies (e.g., MEMBRANE_3, S3L_C0, ROD_2).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description ID Integer Yes - Unique identifier for the element (first token). NODES Array Yes - List of node IDs, e.g., [1, 2, 3]. MATERIAL String Yes - Name of the Material to assign. T Float No* - Alias for thickness. Required for Shells/Membranes. R Float No* - Alias for radius. Required for Rods. LOAD String No - Name of an element Load (e.g., Pressure). CONTACT String No - Contact detection mode: BASIC or EDGE. FRICTION Float No 0.0 Coulomb friction coefficient. FACTOR Float No 1.0 Penalty stiffness factor for contact.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
ELEMENTS TYPE MEMBRANE_3
1  NODES = [1, 2, 3]  MATERIAL = Steel  T = 1.0  CONTACT = EDGE  FRICTION = 0.1
2  NODES = [3, 4, 1]  MATERIAL = Steel  T = 1.0  CONTACT = EDGE  FRICTION = 0.1

ELEMENTS TYPE ROD_2
101 NODES = [10, 11]  MATERIAL = Nylon  R = 0.5

Aliases

The Fembic parser automatically translates legacy short keys like T to thickness and R to radius to maintain compatibility with the core engine.

docs.title: Set
docs.text: Sets are named groups of entities (nodes or elements) used to apply boundary conditions, loads, or to define Sections. They scope entities within one or more physical Parts using explicit ID lists, ranges, or complete part selections.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Entity type: NODE or ELEMENT. part String Yes* - Name of the target Part. Required if parts is not used. parts Array Yes* - List of target Part names. Required if part is not used. ids Array No - Explicit list of node or element IDs. Cannot be combined with range. range Array No - Range definition [start, end, step]. Cannot be combined with ids.

Validation Rules

  • You must specify either part or parts, but not both.
  • You can specify either ids or range, but not both. If neither is specified, the set automatically includes all entities of the specified type within the referenced part(s).
  • For the range parameter, the step (third value) cannot be zero.

docs.title: Range Syntax
docs.text:
The range array follows the pattern: [start_id, end_id, step].

Example: range = [1, 10, 2] will select IDs: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Node set defined by explicit IDs within a single part
[set.FixedNodes]
type = "NODE"
part = "MainPlate"
ids = [1, 2, 10, 15]

# Element set defined by a range across a single part
[set.BottomElements]
type = "ELEMENT"
part = "MainPlate"
range = [1, 100, 1]

# Set targeting all nodes across multiple parts
[set.AllPartNodes]
type = "NODE"
parts = ["MainPlate", "Reinforcement"]

SETS TYPE NODE
FixedNodes NODES = [1, 2, 10, 15]

SETS TYPE ELEMENT
BottomElements RANGE = [1, 100, 1]

docs.title: Surface
docs.text: Surfaces are topological entities created by merging one or more existing Sets. They are primarily used to define interaction boundaries, such as contact zones.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Entity type: NODE or ELEMENT. node_sets Array No* - List of node set names to merge. Required for type NODE. element_sets Array No* - List of element set names to merge. Required for type ELEMENT.

Merging Logic

When you provide multiple sets in the array, COMFOR automatically merges them into a single continuous surface. All referenced sets must exist and match the surface type (e.g., you cannot put a Node Set into an Element Surface).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Creating a master contact surface by merging two element sets
[surface.MasterContactSurface]
type = "ELEMENT"
element_sets = ["TopFlangeElements", "WebElements"]

# Creating a nodal surface for specific output/constraints
[surface.BoundaryInterface]
type = "NODE"
node_sets = ["EdgeNodes_Left", "EdgeNodes_Right"]

SURFACES TYPE ELEMENT
MasterContactSurface ELEMENT_SETS = ["TopFlangeElements", "WebElements"]

SURFACES TYPE NODE
BoundaryInterface NODE_SETS = ["EdgeNodes_Left", "EdgeNodes_Right"]

docs.title: Material
docs.text: The material block defines the constitutive laws and physical properties assigned to the parts of the model. COMFOR supports a variety of models ranging from standard linear elasticity to advanced non-linear textile laws.

docs.title: Common Parameters
docs.text:
These parameters are shared by all material models.

Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Material model keyword: ELASTIC, HYPERELASTIC or HYPERTEXTILE. See Material Module for the specific parameters. density Float Yes - Material density (\(\rho\)). Must be strictly positive. damping Float No 0.0 Mass-proportional Rayleigh damping coefficient (\(\alpha\)). Must be non-negative.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Definition of a standard steel material
[material.Steel_S235]
type = "ELASTIC"
density = 7.8e-9
young = 210000.0
poisson = 0.3
damping = 0.1

MATERIALS TYPE ELASTIC
Steel_S235  DENSITY=7.8E-9  YOUNG=210000.0  POISSON=0.3  DAMPING=0.1

docs.title: Amplitude
docs.text: The amplitude block defines time-dependent functions \(y = f(t)\) used to scale loads, boundary conditions, or other time-sensitive parameters.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Amplitude model: TABULAR. See Amplitude Module. values Array Yes - [time, value] pairs (at least 2), linearly interpolated.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# A simple ramp function from 0 to 10 over 1 second
[amplitude.RampUp]
type = "TABULAR"
values = [
    [0.0, 0.0],
    [1.0, 10.0],
    [2.0, 10.0]
]

Data Format

In Fembic, the values are provided as a flat list. The parser automatically pairs them as [time, value].

AMPLITUDES TYPE TABULAR
RampUp VALUES = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 10.0, 2.0, 10.0]

docs.title: Constraint
docs.text: The constraint block is used to prescribe values to specific degrees of freedom for a group of nodes. This is how you define boundary conditions like fixed supports, imposed velocities, or prescribed rotations.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Constraint technology: BOUNDARY_CONDITION. See Constraint Module. set String Yes - Name of the Node Set where the constraint is applied. preset String No* - "FIXED" blocks all 6 velocities. vx, vy, vz Float or Map No* - Prescribed translational velocities. vrx, vry, vrz Float or Map No* - Prescribed rotational velocities. ax, ay, az Float or Map No* - Prescribed translational accelerations. amplitude String No - Name of a global Amplitude to scale all defined components.

*At least one of preset or a component is required. A component is either a number (vx = 0.0) or a map with its own amplitude (vx = { value = -10.0, amplitude = "Ramp" }).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Simple fixed support using a preset
[constraint.FixedBase]
type = "BOUNDARY_CONDITION"
set = "BottomNodes"
preset = "FIXED"

# Imposed velocity with a local amplitude
[constraint.MovingPlaten]
type = "BOUNDARY_CONDITION"
set = "TopNodes"
vy = { value = -10.0, amplitude = "RampUp" }

CONSTRAINTS TYPE BOUNDARY_CONDITION
FixedBase SET = BottomNodes PRESET = FIXED
MovingPlaten SET = TopNodes VY = -10.0 AMP = RampUp

docs.title: Load
docs.text: The load block defines external efforts applied to the model. These can be punctual forces/moments on nodes, distributed pressures on surfaces, or prescribed body accelerations.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description set String Yes - Name of the Set to apply the load to. amplitude String No - Name of the Amplitude used to scale values. p Float No 0.0 Distributed pressure (typically for Shell/Membrane elements). fx, fy, fz Float No 0.0 Punctual force components along global X, Y, and Z. mx, my, mz Float No 0.0 Punctual moment components around global X, Y, and Z. ax, ay, az Float No 0.0 Linear body acceleration components. arx, ary, arz Float No 0.0 Rotational body acceleration components.

docs.title: Evaluation Logic
docs.text:
The magnitude of a load component at a specific simulation time \(t\) is calculated as the product of the base value and the amplitude factor:

\[F_{applied}(t) = F_{base} \times Amplitude(t)\]

If no amplitude is specified, the scale factor defaults to 1.0.

docs.title: Target Set
docs.text:
• Nodal components (fx...mz, ax...arz) are applied to the nodes of a NODE set.
  • The pressure p is applied to the elements of an ELEMENT set (shell and membrane elements).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Applying a vertical punctual force to a specific set
[load.PunchForce]
set = "TopNodes"
fz = -500.0
amplitude = "RampDown"

# Applying a constant pressure to an element set
[load.InternalPressure]
set = "InnerElements"
p = 10.5

# Gravity (body acceleration) on all the nodes of a part
[load.Gravity]
set = "AllNodes"
az = -9810.0

LOADS
PunchForce SET = TopNodes FZ = -500.0 AMPLITUDE = RampDown

LOADS
InternalPressure SET = InnerElements P = 10.5

Multi-Component Loads

A single load block can define multiple components (e.g., fx, fy, and fz) simultaneously. All values in the block share the same amplitude.

docs.title: Contact Behaviour
docs.text: The contact_behaviour block defines the physical laws (Normal and Tangential) that govern the interaction between two surfaces. These laws must be defined by name so they can be assigned to a specific Contact pair.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Technology keyword. Normal laws: LINEAR_PENALTY, PENALTY_ADHESION. Tangential law: COULOMB. See Contact Behaviour Module for their parameters.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Definition of a normal penalty law
[contact_behaviour.HardContact]
type = "LINEAR_PENALTY"
stiffness = 1.0e6

# Definition of a tangential friction law
[contact_behaviour.SteelFriction]
type = "COULOMB"
mu = 0.15

CONTACT_BEHAVIOURS TYPE LINEAR_PENALTY
HardContact STIFFNESS = 1.0e6

CONTACT_BEHAVIOURS TYPE COULOMB
SteelFriction MU = 0.15

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: The contact block defines the interaction between geometric entities. It couples surfaces or the whole domain with specific physical laws defined in the Contact Behaviour section.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Interaction technology keyword: PAIR or GENERAL. master String Yes* - Name of the first Surface. Required for type PAIR if surfaces is not used. slave String Yes* - Name of the second Surface. Required for type PAIR if surfaces is not used. surfaces Array Yes* - List of two surfaces ["Surf1", "Surf2"]. Alternative syntax for type PAIR. normal String Yes - Name of the assigned Normal Contact Behaviour. tangential String Yes - Name of the assigned Tangential Contact Behaviour. edge Boolean No false If true, enables edge contact detection for PAIR contact.

The same surface can be used as master and slave to define self-contact.

Surface Definition Rules

  • For PAIR contact, define surfaces using either the master/slave pair or the surfaces array.
  • For GENERAL contact, surface definitions are omitted as it applies globally. Only one GENERAL contact can be defined per model; it can be combined with PAIR contacts.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Contact Pair defined using Master/Slave keywords
[contact.DieToBlank]
type = "PAIR"
master = "ToolSurface"
slave = "WorkpieceNodes"
normal = "HardPenalty"
tangential = "SteelFriction"

# General contact definition
[contact.GlobalContact]
type = "GENERAL"
normal = "SoftPenalty"
tangential = "FabricFriction"

CONTACTS TYPE PAIR
DieToBlank MASTER = ToolSurface SLAVE = WorkpieceNodes NORMAL = HardPenalty TANGENTIAL = SteelFriction

CONTACTS TYPE GENERAL
GlobalContact NORMAL = SoftPenalty TANGENTIAL = FabricFriction

docs.title: Tracker
docs.text: The tracker block logs discrete simulation data into separate CSV files, named <result_root>/<tracker_name>.csv. It is the primary tool for extracting nodal history or element state variables over time. Values are written each time an output frame is written.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Entity type to track: NODE or ELEMENT. variable String Yes - Physical quantity to log. See Tracker Module. set String Yes* - Name of the target Set. Cannot be combined with nodes/elements. nodes Array Yes* - Explicit node IDs (NODE trackers). elements Array Yes* - Explicit element IDs (ELEMENT trackers). direction String Yes* - "X", "Y" or "Z". Required for NODE trackers. component String Yes* - Component of the variable (e.g. "xx", "warp", "value"). Required for ELEMENT trackers. See Tracker Module.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Tracking the reaction force of a node set in the Z direction
[tracker.ReactionForce]
type = "NODE"
variable = "FORCE"
direction = "Z"
set = "BottomNodes"

# Tracking the Cauchy stress xx on explicit elements
[tracker.CoreStress]
type = "ELEMENT"
variable = "CAUCHY_STRESS"
component = "xx"
elements = [101, 102]

TRACKERS TYPE NODE
ReactionForce SET = BottomNodes VARIABLE = FORCE DIRECTION = Z

TRACKERS TYPE ELEMENT
CoreStress ELEMENTS = [101, 102] VARIABLE = CAUCHY_STRESS COMPONENT = xx

docs.title: Solver
docs.text:
TOML Only

This block is specific to the TOML configuration format. The Fembic format uses implicit solver parameters.

The optional solver block configures the dynamics solver used for time integration. COMFOR currently implements an explicit solver with centered differences integration. If the block is omitted, the explicit solver is used with the default values below. Only one solver block is allowed.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description type String No "EXPLICIT" Solver type. Supported value: "EXPLICIT". integrator String No "central_difference" Time integrator type. Supported value: "central_difference". time_step_factor Float No 0.9 Safety factor for automatic time step calculation. energy_balance_epsilon Float No 1.0e-2 Tolerance for energy balance verification.

Automatic Time Step Calculation

If the time step is not specified in the control block, COMFOR automatically calculates a stable time step based on mesh and material properties. The time_step_factor is applied to this critical time step: \(\Delta t = \alpha \cdot \Delta t_{crit}\) where \(\alpha\) is the safety factor.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Explicit solver configuration with automatic time stepping
[solver]
type = "EXPLICIT"
integrator = "central_difference"
time_step_factor = 0.9
energy_balance_epsilon = 1.0e-2

# Only change the safety factor, other values keep their default
[solver]
time_step_factor = 0.8

Implicit Parameters

In Fembic format, the explicit solver is used by default with predefined parameters. It is not possible to explicitly configure the solver in this format.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
COMFOR validates the whole input file before building the model, and reports all the errors found at once (in the terminal and in the job log). To only validate a file, without running the simulation:

comfor -j simulation.toml --validate

The validation checks:

  • the TOML syntax (with the line number of the error);
  • the presence of the required blocks (control, at least one output) and of the name of each block;
  • the uniqueness of the names within each block type;
  • the mandatory parameters of each block, their types and their allowed values or ranges (e.g. thickness > 0, poisson in \([0, 0.5]\), run_from < run_to);
  • the exclusive options (translation/pattern, ids/range, part/parts, set/nodes...).

Cross-references between blocks (a section referencing a material, an assignment referencing a set, a contact referencing surfaces...) and the compatibility between element types and sections are checked when the model is built, at the beginning of the simulation. See Running the Analysis for details.

  1. Parsing, syntax analysis, or syntactic analysis is the process of analyzing a string of symbols, either in natural language, computer languages or data structures, conforming to the rules of a formal grammar. Wikipedia ↩

docs.title: Amplitudes
docs.text:
• Tabular

This section provides a practical overview of the time-dependent amplitude models available in COMFOR. Amplitudes are used to scale boundary conditions, loads, or other time-sensitive parameters over simulation time.

docs.title: Common Parameters for All Amplitudes
docs.text:
Every amplitude block requires these base parameters:

Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Amplitude formulation keyword (e.g., TABULAR).

docs.title: Tabular
docs.text: The TABULAR amplitude type defines a temporal curve \(y = f(t)\) through a set of discrete time/value pairs. COMFOR performs linear interpolation between the defined points.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description values Array Yes List of discrete [time, value] pairs. Must contain at least 2 pairs.

Operational Logic

  • Linear Interpolation: Evaluated linearly between consecutive points \((t_1, v_1)\) and \((t_2, v_2)\).
  • Out-of-Bounds: If the current simulation time \(t\) is outside the defined range \([t_{\text{min}}, t_{\text{max}}]\), the amplitude returns 0.0.
  • Automatic Sorting: COMFOR automatically sorts time points in ascending order during initialization.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# A ramp load increasing from 0.0 to 10.0 over 1 second, held constant until 2.0s
[amplitude.RampUp]
type = "TABULAR"
values = [
    [0.0, 0.0],
    [1.0, 10.0],
    [2.0, 10.0]
]

AMPLITUDES TYPE TABULAR
RampUp VALUES = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 10.0, 2.0, 10.0]

docs.title: Choose an Amplitude Model
docs.text: • Use TABULAR for experimental loading curves, punch velocity profiles, or step-wise boundary condition scaling.

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• Boundary Condition

This section provides a practical overview of the constraint formulations available in COMFOR. Constraints are used to prescribe boundary conditions (velocities or accelerations) on designated node sets.

docs.title: Common Parameters for All Constraints
docs.text:
Every constraint block requires these base parameters:

Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Constraint formulation keyword (e.g., BOUNDARY_CONDITION). set String Yes - Name of the target Node Set. amplitude String No - Name of a global Amplitude applied to all components.

docs.title: Boundary Condition
docs.text: The BOUNDARY_CONDITION constraint prescribes nodal velocities (\(v\)) and accelerations (\(a\)). Component values can be defined as flat numbers or as nested inline maps to assign individual local amplitudes.

docs.title: Component Syntax
docs.text:
Each kinematic component (e.g., vx, vry, az) can be specified in two ways:

  1. Numeric: vx = 1.0 (Scales with the block-level global amplitude if defined).
  2. Inline Map: vx = { value = 1.0, amplitude = "LocalAmp" } (Overrides with a specific local amplitude).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Category Description preset Special Set to "FIXED" to fix all 6 degrees of freedom (\(v_x, v_y, v_z, v_{rx}, v_{ry}, v_{rz} = 0.0\)). vx, vy, vz Linear Velocity Prescribed velocity along global X, Y, or Z axes. vrx, vry, vrz Rotational Velocity Prescribed angular velocity around global X, Y, or Z axes. ax, ay, az Acceleration Prescribed linear acceleration along global X, Y, or Z axes.

Velocity vs. Acceleration Priority

If a velocity component (e.g., vx) is set for a given axis, any prescribed acceleration for the same axis (ax) is overridden and set to \(0.0\) to guarantee kinematic consistency.

docs.title: Evaluation Logic
docs.text:
The prescribed value for a given component at simulation time \(t\) is calculated as:

\[V_{\text{applied}}(t) = \text{Value} \times \text{Amplitude}(t)\]
  • If a component specifies its own local amplitude, that local amplitude is evaluated.
  • If no local amplitude is defined, it falls back to the block-level global amplitude.
  • If neither is provided, the scale factor defaults to 1.0.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
# Fixed base support using the FIXED preset
[constraint.FixedBase]
type = "BOUNDARY_CONDITION"
set = "BottomNodes"
preset = "FIXED"

# Prescribed platen displacement with local and global amplitudes
[constraint.MovingPlaten]
type = "BOUNDARY_CONDITION"
set = "TopNodes"
amplitude = "GlobalRamp"
vy = { value = -10.0, amplitude = "LocalRamp" }
vz = 0.0

CONSTRAINTS TYPE BOUNDARY_CONDITION
FixedBase SET = BottomNodes PRESET = FIXED

CONSTRAINTS TYPE BOUNDARY_CONDITION
MovingPlaten SET = TopNodes VY = -10.0 AMP = LocalRamp VZ = 0.0

docs.title: Choose a Constraint Type
docs.text:
• Use BOUNDARY_CONDITION with preset = "FIXED" for rigid clamps and fixed boundaries.
  • Use BOUNDARY_CONDITION with prescribed vx/vy/vz velocities and a Tabular Amplitude for forming tool motion or platen displacement.

docs.title: Contact Behaviours
docs.text:
• Normal Laws

  • Tangential Laws

This section provides a practical overview of the physical laws governing surface interaction in COMFOR. Contact behaviours are defined independently and referenced by Contact blocks.

docs.title: Common Parameters for All Contact Behaviours
docs.text:
Every contact behaviour block requires this base parameter:

Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Contact law technology keyword (LINEAR_PENALTY, PENALTY_ADHESION, COULOMB).

docs.title: Normal Contact Laws
docs.text: Normal contact laws compute reaction forces perpendicular to the interface to prevent penetration or manage adhesion.

docs.title: LINEAR_PENALTY
docs.text:
A linear penalty spring model that applies a normal compressive force proportional to the penetration distance (gap).

Parameter Type Required Description stiffness Float Yes Penalty spring stiffness. Must be strictly positive. (Alias: factor)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[contact_behaviour.HardNormal]
type = "LINEAR_PENALTY"
stiffness = 1.0e6

CONTACT_BEHAVIOURS TYPE LINEAR_PENALTY
HardNormal STIFFNESS = 1.0e6

docs.title: PENALTY_ADHESION
docs.text:
A normal law that handles both compression penalty forces during penetration and tensile adhesive forces during separation.

Parameter Type Required Description stiffness Float Yes Compression penalty stiffness. Must be strictly positive. (Alias: factor) strength Float Yes Adhesive force magnitude per unit area. Must be non-negative. (Alias: adhesive_strength) threshold Float No Distance tolerance for adhesion. Defaults to element thickness (\(t\)). (Alias: adhesion_threshold)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[contact_behaviour.AdhesiveTool]
type = "PENALTY_ADHESION"
stiffness = 1.0e6
strength = 50.0
threshold = 0.5

CONTACT_BEHAVIOURS TYPE PENALTY_ADHESION
AdhesiveTool STIFFNESS = 1.0e6 STRENGTH = 50.0 THRESHOLD = 0.5

docs.title: Tangential Contact Laws
docs.text: Tangential contact laws compute friction forces parallel to the contact plane.

docs.title: COULOMB
docs.text:
Standard Coulomb friction law. It applies a tangential force proportional to the normal contact force and the friction coefficient \(\mu\).

Parameter Type Required Description friction Float Yes Friction coefficient \(\mu\). Must be non-negative. (Alias: mu)

Regularization & Smooth Factor

To minimize numerical oscillations during abrupt changes in slip direction, the COULOMB implementation uses a continuous smoothing factor derived from the dot product of consecutive slip vectors.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[contact_behaviour.SteelFriction]
type = "COULOMB"
friction = 0.15

CONTACT_BEHAVIOURS TYPE COULOMB
SteelFriction FRICTION = 0.15

docs.title: Choose a Contact Behaviour
docs.text:
• Use LINEAR_PENALTY (Normal) + COULOMB (Tangential) for standard tool-part or self-contact interfaces.
  • Use PENALTY_ADHESION (Normal) for sticky tools, tack analysis, or resin-rich composite forming.

docs.title: Elements
docs.text:
• 1D Elements

  • Shell & Membrane

  • Contact Elements

This section provides a practical overview of the finite element formulations available in COMFOR. Physical properties (such as material or thickness) are assigned to elements indirectly via Sections and Section Assignments.

docs.title: Common Parameters for All Elements
docs.text:
All element definitions require the nodes array defining connectivity.

Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Element formulation keyword. nodes Array Yes - Array of node IDs defining element connectivity. contact String No - Internal contact detection trigger: "BASIC" or "EDGE". load String No - Optional name of a Load target.

TOML

In TOML, elements are created from a mesh: the type comes from the mesh reader (possibly changed with element_mapping) and the connectivity from the mesh file. Loads are applied with load blocks on element sets, and contact with contact blocks. The contact and load element parameters are only used by the legacy Fembic format.

docs.title: 1D Elements
docs.text: 1D structural elements model axial bar/truss behavior along line connectivity.

docs.title: ROD_2
docs.text:
2-node linear rod/truss element supporting axial tension and compression.

Parameter Value / Range Description Nodes 2 Node connectivity array [N1, N2]. Required Section ROD Requires a section with a defined radius and material. Contact Support "EDGE" Generates an internal CONTACT_LINE for edge contact detection.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
TOML 
[mesh.InlineBar]
type = "INLINE"
nodes = [ [1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [2, 10.0, 0.0, 0.0] ]
elements = [ [1, "ROD_2", 1, 2] ]

docs.title: 2D Shell & Membrane Elements
docs.text: 2D surface element formulations for membranes and thin shells.

docs.title: MEMBRANE_3
docs.text:
3-node triangular membrane element with in-plane stiffness and no bending resistance.

Parameter Value / Range Description Nodes 3 Node connectivity array [N1, N2, N3]. Required Section MEMBRANE Requires a section with thickness and material. Contact Support "BASIC", "EDGE" Generates internal CONTACT_TRIANGLE (and CONTACT_LINE for "EDGE").

docs.title: S3L_C0
docs.text:
3-node triangular shell element with \(C^0\) continuous linear bending formulation.

Parameter Value / Range Description Nodes 3 Node connectivity array [N1, N2, N3]. Required Section SHELL_GAUSS, SHELL_GENERALIZED Requires a shell section with thickness and material (plus nip for SHELL_GAUSS). Contact Support "BASIC", "EDGE" Generates internal contact entities.

docs.title: DKT18
docs.text:
3-node Discrete Kirchhoff Triangle (DKT) element for thin shell bending analysis.

Parameter Value / Range Description Nodes 3 Node connectivity array [N1, N2, N3]. Required Section SHELL_GAUSS, SHELL_GENERALIZED Requires a shell section with thickness and material (plus nip for SHELL_GAUSS). Contact Support "BASIC", "EDGE" Generates internal contact entities.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[mesh.Plate]
type = "INLINE"
nodes = [
    [1, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
    [2, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
    [3, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0]
]
elements = [
    [1, "DKT18", 1, 2, 3]
]

ELEMENTS TYPE DKT18
1 NODES = [1, 2, 3]

docs.title: Contact Elements
docs.text: Specialized contact elements automatically generated or explicitly defined to enforce contact boundary conditions.

docs.title: CONTACT_TRIANGLE
docs.text:
3-node surface contact triangle element.

Parameter Value / Range Description Nodes 3 Node connectivity array [N1, N2, N3]. Required Section RIGID Linked to a rigid section defining physical thickness and geometry ("SHELL" or "SOLID").

docs.title: CONTACT_LINE
docs.text:
2-node line contact element for edge-to-edge or node-to-edge interaction.

Parameter Value / Range Description Nodes 2 Node connectivity array [N1, N2]. Required Section RIGID Linked to a rigid section defining thickness (used as contact radius \(r = t/2\)).

Contact Parameters Deprecation

In COMFOR TOML, penalty factors (factor) and friction coefficients (friction) are no longer specified directly on elements. They must be configured in Contact Behaviour blocks and assigned via Contact Pairs.

docs.title: Choose an Element Type
docs.text:
• Use MEMBRANE_3 for thin dry fabrics or films where bending stiffness is negligible.
  • Use DKT18 or S3L_C0 for thin shell structures requiring out-of-plane bending and curvature calculations.
  • Use ROD_2 for 1D structural members or edge reinforcements.
  • Use contact = "BASIC" or contact = "EDGE" on structural elements to automatically instantiate underlying contact geometry.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
• Elastic

  • Hyperelastic

  • Composite

This section provides a practical overview of the material models available in COMFOR. For detailed theoretical background and mathematical formulations, refer to the Theory section.

docs.title: Common Parameters for All Materials
docs.text:
Every material block requires these base parameters regardless of the underlying constitutive law.

Parameter Type Required Default Description type String Yes - Material model keyword (ELASTIC, HYPERELASTIC, HYPERTEXTILE). density Float Yes - Mass density (\(\rho\)). Must be strictly positive. damping Float No 0.0 Mass-proportional Rayleigh damping coefficient (\(\alpha\)). Must be non-negative.

docs.title: Elastic Models
docs.text: Standard isotropic linear elasticity based on Hooke's Law (Saint-Venant-Kirchhoff formulation). It assumes a plane stress state for 2D elements and is suitable for small strains with large rotations.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Range Description young Float Yes \(>0\) Young's Modulus (\(E\)). poisson Float Yes \([0, 0.5]\) Poisson's ratio (\(\nu\)).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[material.Steel_S235]
type = "ELASTIC"
density = 7.8e-9
young = 210000.0
poisson = 0.3
damping = 0.1

MATERIALS TYPE ELASTIC
Steel_S235 DENSITY = 7.8e-9 YOUNG = 210000.0 POISSON = 0.3 DAMPING = 0.1

docs.title: Hyperelastic Models
docs.text: Non-linear elastic models designed for materials undergoing finite strains (large deformations), such as rubbers or soft membranes. Currently supports the Ogden strain energy potential for incompressible materials.

docs.title: Parameters (Ogden)
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Description potential String Yes Potential model type. Must be set to OGDEN. mu Array Yes List of shear moduli \(\mu_i\). alpha Array Yes List of non-linear dimensionless exponents \(\alpha_i\).

Array Consistency

The mu and alpha arrays must have the exact same number of entries. Each pair \((\mu_i, \alpha_i)\) defines one term of the Ogden strain energy potential.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[material.Rubber]
type = "HYPERELASTIC"
potential = "OGDEN"
density = 1.1e-9
mu = [ -0.09, 13.9, -0.20 ]
alpha = [ -13.7, 0.10, 5.06 ]

MATERIALS TYPE HYPERELASTIC
Rubber DENSITY = 1.1e-9 POTENTIAL = OGDEN MU = [-0.09, 13.9, -0.20] ALPHA = [-13.7, 0.10, 5.06]

docs.title: Composite (Hypertextile)
docs.text: Designed for anisotropic textile materials (e.g., dry or impregnated woven composites). It is an advanced invariant-based model (HYPERTEXTILE) that decouples fiber elongation in warp and weft directions from in-plane shear and out-of-plane bending.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Required Default Description warp_orientation Array Yes - Initial warp fiber unit vector \([x, y, z]\). weft_orientation Array Yes - Initial weft fiber unit vector \([x, y, z]\). k_elong_warp Array Yes - Polynomial coefficients for warp elongation stiffness. k_elong_weft Array Yes - Polynomial coefficients for weft elongation stiffness. k_shear Array Yes - Polynomial coefficients for in-plane shear stiffness. k_bend_warp Array No - Optional polynomial coefficients for warp bending moments. k_bend_weft Array No - Optional polynomial coefficients for weft bending moments. k_bend_twist Array No - Optional polynomial coefficients for twisting stiffness.

Orientation Projection

During initialization, COMFOR automatically projects the global orientation vectors onto the local basis of each element. If a fiber direction is found to be perpendicular to an element's plane, the simulation will stop with a validation error.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
TOML Fembic 
[material.CarbonFabric]
type = "HYPERTEXTILE"
